example_prompt: Screen a person's full name against sanctions, PEP and adverse-media lists and get the One-Time AML result in the same HTTP response, without hosting a webhook.

user_id.description: Partner-provided user identifier. Optional in general; required when `search_existing_user` is `true`. Reconciled with the `User-ID` header and any token-bound user id after authentication — disagreement is a 403. Generated automatically as a TypeID when omitted everywhere.

countries.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes (uppercase) to screen against. Remains authoritative for the screening even when `search_existing_user` is `true`. Sent as a JSON-encoded array string in the multipart part (e.g. `["NG","KE"]`).

full_name.description: Full name to screen. Remains authoritative for the screening — never replaced or compared with prior enrollee information, even when `search_existing_user` is `true`.

birth_year.description: Optional four-digit birth year, minimum 1000 and maximum the current UTC year. A bare integer is also accepted. Full dates, decimals, non-four-digit values, and future years are rejected.

strict_match.description: Optional. When `true` (default), uses the stricter match filter set; when `false`, uses a looser filter set. Accepts standard multipart boolean string representations (`"true"`/`"false"`). Always echoed back on the callback.

aliases.description: Optional list of alternate names to screen, at most 20 entries, each at most 256 characters. Sent as a JSON-encoded array string in the multipart part (e.g. `["Johnny Doe"]`).

search_existing_user.description: Optional. A gate, not a data source: when `true`, requires the resolved `user_id` to belong to a partner-scoped, non-deleted enrollee with at least one non-expired prior KYC record carrying a usable name and country. It never overwrites `full_name`, `countries`, or `birth_year` — those stay authoritative. Accepts standard multipart boolean string representations.

granted.description: Must be true; user has granted consent.

granted_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when consent was granted.

notice_language.description: ISO 639-1 language code of the privacy notice shown, uppercase.

notice_privacy_policy_url.description: HTTPS URL of the privacy policy notice shown to the user.

user_details.description: Consumer-stated PII fields for the screened user. Either email or phone_number must be provided.

last_name.description: Last name / surname of the individual.

email.description: Email address. At least one of email or phone_number is required.

phone_number.description: Phone number in E.164 format (must start with +). At least one of email or phone_number is required.

callback_url.description: Optional here. If you supply one it is stored so POST /v3/replay/{job_id} can use it later, but no webhook is ever sent — the result is in this response.

partner_params.description: Arbitrary key-value metadata for partner reference.

source_sdk.description: Source SDK identifier. Can also be provided via the `SmileID-Source-SDK` header.

source_sdk_version.description: Source SDK version. Can also be provided via the `SmileID-Source-SDK-Version` header.

input_schema.description: multipart/form-data. countries, aliases, consent, user_details, partner_params and metadata are JSON-encoded strings in their form parts. Optional header SmileID-Idempotency-Key: Opaque key, 16 to 128 characters of `A-Z a-z 0-9 - _`, that makes a submission safe to repeat. The job id is derived from it, so a request carrying a key you have already used resolves to that same job: it returns the original result and screens — and bills — nothing a second time. Send one whenever you might retry, since a retry without a key starts a new, separately billed screening.

reason.description: Canonical machine-readable reason. `null` for a clear outcome.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp the screening job started processing.

completed_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp the terminal outcome was reached. Omitted only if the terminal state could not be read.

partner_params.description: Partner-supplied key-value metadata, with internal transport keys (`_sandbox_v3`, `job_id`, `job_type`, `user_id`) stripped. `null` when empty.

kyc_receipt.description: Signed receipt URL. `null` on submission; populated for `clear`, `block`, and `attention` outcomes. Remains `null` for `error`.

strict_match.description: The resolved `strict_match` value used for the screening.

items.description: A single sanctions/PEP/adverse-media hit. Public snake_case fields only — internal provider references (e.g. sigma_ref) are always stripped before the callback is sent.

addresses.description: Known addresses, each a single string of the form `<address> <country>` (webhook page; the OpenAPI types the items as objects).

news_summary.description: Per-category summary of the person's news-media exposure. The raw article list the provider returns under `adverse_media` is never included in the callback; a screening whose only hits are news media resolves to `attention` / `news_media_match`.

aliases.description: Alternate names and spellings recorded for the entity.

dates_of_birth.description: Recorded dates of birth, as strings (webhook page; the OpenAPI types the items as objects).

nationalities.description: Recorded nationalities, as strings (webhook page; the OpenAPI types the items as objects).

pep_level.description: The PEP tier, `1` being the most senior. `null` when the entity is not a PEP. integer | null in the OpenAPI, string | null on the webhook page.

political_positions.description: Political positions held. Each entry has `position` and, where known, `country`, `from`, and `to` (webhook page).

ref.description: Smile ID's reference for this person within the result set (webhook page).

consent.description: ISO 27560 consent record for the granted consent.

antifraud.description: Antifraud risk assessment. `null` when no scored fraud result exists for the job.

device_signals.description: Device/network signals captured at submission time. Always `null` for an `error` outcome, and best-effort `null` when no metadata was captured.

gotchas: Two-step auth: first call POST /v3/token with headers SmileID-Partner-ID and SmileID-API-Key (SMILEID_PARTNER_ID / SMILEID_API_KEY) to get a JWT, then send SmileID-Partner-ID and SmileID-Token: {token} on this request. The token expires 15 minutes after issuance — Smile ID recommends minting a new one for every verification request rather than reusing it. Never mint tokens in the browser: the API key must stay on your backend.
The Authentication page requires both SmileID-Partner-ID and SmileID-Token on all V3 requests; the endpoint's own OpenAPI only declares SmileID-Token. Send both.

The body must be multipart/form-data, not JSON (415 otherwise). countries and aliases (per this endpoint's docs), and consent, user_details and partner_params (as on the other V3 endpoints) are sent as JSON-serialised strings in their form part — e.g. form.append('consent', JSON.stringify({...})).
consent is mandatory in V3: granted must be true, granted_at an ISO 8601 timestamp, notice_language an uppercase ISO 639-1 code (e.g. 'FR'), notice_privacy_policy_url an https URL.

countries is required and sent as a JSON-encoded array string (e.g. '["CI","SN"]'); full_name is the name actually screened — user_details is still required (given_names, last_name and email or phone_number).

Send a SmileID-Idempotency-Key (16-128 chars of A-Z a-z 0-9 - _) whenever you might retry: a retry without a key starts a new, separately billed screening. Reuse the same key only when you got no response at all (network failure, gateway timeout): it resolves to the same job and returns the original result instead of screening again.

Slower than the async /v3/aml: screening runs inline under a request deadline. 408 means the screening provider did not answer in time — the job exists and is terminal in 'error', nothing is billed, and GET /v3/status/{jobId} will only ever return that error: resubmit (with a new idempotency key) rather than poll. A screening that fails internally is a 500, not a 200 with status 'error'.

GET /v3/status/{jobId} (SmileID-Job-ID response header) only returns the status, not people[] — keep the 200 body, or store a callback_url and use replay_verification_webhook to get the full result again.
A 200 response carries Response-Signature and Response-Timestamp headers computed like the webhooks' — verify them the same way.
status 'attention' with reason 'news_media_match' means only adverse-media hits were found; the raw article list is never included, only people[].news_summary.
402 Insufficient wallet balance — top up the Smile ID wallet from the Dashboard before retrying.

Sandbox base URL is https://testapi.smileidentity.com (this spec uses production, https://api.smileidentity.com). Keys, tokens and callback URLs are environment-specific: a sandbox token returns 401 in production. Sandbox only accepts the documented AML test identities, matched on full_name alone — user_details play no part in matching; production rejects test identities with 400.
